metadata.title: Recover distributed institutional intention from the deliberate/conspiratorial false binary
metadata.notes: Reference proposal demonstrating anomaly-driven concept formation without deleting either established term.

trigger.summary: Multiple reasoning episodes forced intentional but decentralized institutional conduct into either conspiracy or accident.

observedResiduals.description: Several institutions intentionally selected compatible framings without evidence of a secret command structure.
observedResiduals.consequence: The system could not attribute local responsibility without overstating coordination.

observedResiduals.description: Actors continued choices after the aggregate effect became foreseeable, although no actor controlled the whole system.
observedResiduals.consequence: Foreseeability and continued participation disappeared from the causal account.

observedResiduals.description: Organizations independently converged on the same salience strategy because incentives and risk structures aligned.
observedResiduals.consequence: A recurrent middle mechanism remained unnamed and therefore difficult to compare across domains.

diagnosis.rationale: The recurrent residuals are not noise. They identify a missing interpretive resource spanning intention, coordination, and system-level emergence.

change.intent: Make intentional decentralized conduct representable while preserving conspiracy and accident as narrower concepts.

atomicChanges.description: Register distributed institutional intention as a legitimate middle-space concept.
Link local intention to global emergence without equating emergence with accident.
Require evidence of concealed multi-party coordination before asserting conspiracy.

resultingConcepts.label: Distributed institutional intention
resultingConcepts.definition: Deliberate choices by multiple institutions whose interaction produces a system-level pattern without a single concealed command structure.

resultingConcepts.label: Parallel incentive alignment
resultingConcepts.definition: Independent adoption of similar strategies because incentives, constraints, or risk structures converge.

resultingConcepts.label: Anticipated emergence
resultingConcepts.definition: A system-level effect that participants foresee and continue contributing to without centrally controlling it.

plurality.sharedCore: All viewpoints distinguish intentional conduct, coordination evidence, and aggregate system effects, but weight them differently.

localInterpretations.interpretation: Conspiracy remains a narrow claim requiring evidence of agreement or coordination; local intent is assessed separately.
Organizations can intentionally optimize local objectives that combine into a harmful global pattern.
People need a usable middle vocabulary between secret plot and nobody chose anything.

translationRules.rule: Translate claims of distributed intention into actor-specific decisions and effects; do not translate them into agreement without coordination evidence.
translationRules.lossWarning: Systemic responsibility may be understated when only agreement-based legal categories are available.

translationRules.rule: Resolve broad words such as deliberate into actor, decision, scope, incentive, and interaction fields.
translationRules.lossWarning: Over-formalization can erase the practical pattern the ordinary descriptor was naming.

alternatives.description: Keep conspiracy/accident as the only options and add prose disclaimers.
alternatives.rationale: The failure is representational, so prose warnings do not give agents a type they can preserve, query, or validate.

alternatives.description: Broaden conspiracy until it includes all deliberate institutional interaction.
alternatives.rationale: This destroys the useful narrower meaning of concealed coordination and reproduces the category collapse in the opposite direction.

alternatives.description: Use a shared umbrella term across legal, institutional, and public viewpoints without adding middle concepts.
alternatives.rationale: Boundary translation is useful, but the recurring causal mechanisms still require explicit concepts.

competencyQuestions: Can Atlas represent intentional institutional conduct without asserting secret coordination?
Can the ecology distinguish evidence of local intent, inter-organizational coordination, foreseeability, and global emergence?
Can Forge retain responsibility-relevant facts when the conspiracy threshold is not met?
counterexamples: Independent firms deliberately copy a visible pricing strategy without communicating.
A concealed agreement among firms remains conspiratorial even when its market effect would also have emerged from incentives.
A one-off accidental synchronization lacks the repeated intentional local choices required for distributed institutional intention.
proofObligations.rollbackPlan: Remove the experimental bindings and restore the previous registry version; retain the proposal, evidence, and test receipts as historical records.
proofObligations.migrationPlan: Map existing claims tagged conspiracy-or-accident into unresolved candidates, then reclassify only after actor-level intent and coordination evidence are reviewed.
proofObligations.ordinaryPersonTest: A reader without systems terminology should be able to distinguish secret plot, deliberate decentralized conduct, and accident in blind examples.
proofObligations.consistencyIllusionMitigation: Audit reasoning paths separately from answer agreement and preserve any agent that identifies actor-level intent without coordination evidence.

review.rationale: The proposal is sufficiently grounded for branch-level experimentation but must earn canonical promotion through competency tests and observed reduction in category collapse.
